topic: Certified exact-risk weighted-random-isolation design for network total effects. For a fixed directed interference graph, its undirected WRI conflict graph C_G, bounded positive integer priority weights, fixed full-neighborhood potential outcomes, and a prespecified finite rule library, write the RDIM error as a 2n-dimensional random linear form and compute each dense risk matrix Q_l exactly. Prove an output-sensitive L n^2 2^{O(w log(w+1))} poly(n,b) algorithm from a width-w tree decomposition by integrating priority-order and reciprocal-count messages, including correctness and bit complexity. Over the graph ellipsoid defined by diag((I+gamma L_C)^{-1},(I+gamma L_C)^{-1}), return the minimax rule mixture, least-favourable endpoint distribution, and primal-dual optimality certificate. For arbitrary graphs give simultaneous operator-norm Monte Carlo regions and a certified worst-case-risk gap. Consumer: a universal-financial-education versus none follow-up to Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet's rural-China insurance diffusion experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Every RDIM risk entry was reduced to one- and two-marked isolated-set count probabilities, including odd counts and bias. Integer-weight risks have polynomial output bit length, and a three-state polynomial recurrence was derived and checked by exact enumeration on three forests and 344 matrix entries. Two bidirected three-leaf stars force isolated-set size two; reciprocal hub/leaf rules produce distinct verified risks. Checks covered local-max versus sequential greedy semantics, directed-star legality, parity denominators, rationality, PSD ellipsoid, generic SDP reduction, treewidth hardness, and recent design papers. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Compress joined separator priority/count messages to 2^{O(w log(w+1))} poly(n,b) size; the direct construction retains (nb)^{O(w)} coefficients and proves only XP complexity. EARLY KILL TEST: On all width-two/three graphs with n≤9 and weights in {1,2,3}, compare every tagged coefficient with exhaustive priority ordering, then derive the symbolic message-size recurrence; any unavoidable (nb)^w factor or parameter-preserving hardness obstruction kills the promised FPT kernel and forces pivot. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_awri_mixture_minimax_certificate.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact RDIM risk requires joint tracking of two marked vertices, final isolated-set size, odd-count effects, and reciprocal treatment/control denominators. The prior construction compresses independent cluster labels into size-stratum histogram polynomials, but a WRI tree-decomposition join must synchronize separator priority order, domination history, and count-generating data across both children. Direct coefficient tables retain an (nb)^{O(w)} factor, while the linear-extension result shows that apparently similar order-counting problems can be W[1]-hard under the wrong graph parameter. The missing object is therefore either a separator equivalence relation that removes dependence on n and b or a parameter-preserving obstruction showing that no such compression exists.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A dichotomy theorem giving either a proved message invariant and join recurrence of size 2^{O(w log(w+1))} poly(n,b), with exact rational reconstruction and polynomial output-bit length for every Q_l entry, or a #W[1]/W[1]-hardness reduction parameterized by w for a required marked moment.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing WRI work compares individual weights through a surrogate, while nearby network-design work optimizes cluster partitions or bounds unrestricted minimax risk. The prior finite-orbit saddle certificate uses posterior means and cellwise Bayes-risk equalities; for a graph ellipsoid, the first proof step changes to maximizing a continuous quadratic form, making the dual adversary a PSD trace-one matrix rather than a finite response-orbit prior. A complete theorem must turn that spectral dual into a least-favourable endpoint distribution and establish complementary slackness without assuming every rule receives positive weight or the top eigenvalue is simple.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact primal-dual SDP theorem for min_{p in Delta_L} lambda_max(D^{1/2}(sum_l p_l Q_l)D^{1/2}) that returns optimal rule probabilities, an attaining distribution on ellipsoid-boundary endpoints, equality of game values, and necessary-and-sufficient support and eigenspace conditions.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior concentration argument is scalar and depends on a fixed local footprint, whereas changing one WRI priority can trigger a long sequential-greedy cascade. Randomized-clustering work shows that design-law probabilities can be estimated offline, and matrix Bernstein controls independent matrix averages, but neither result constructs an unbiased self-adjoint contribution for RDIM's random reciprocal denominators, odd counts, and bias terms. Entrywise intervals are insufficient because ellipsoidal worst-case risk is spectral, and the chosen mixture is data-dependent; coverage must therefore hold jointly for all library matrices before being propagated through the eigenvalue minimax problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem giving computable radii r_l(N,delta), simultaneous coverage Pr{forall l: ||Qhat_l-Q_l||op <= r_l} >= 1-delta, explicit simulation complexity, and primal-dual upper and lower bounds certifying the selected mixture's excess ellipsoidal worst-case RDIM risk.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Ellipsoidal worst-case risk is Lipschitz in operator norm, so this concentration machinery controls the perturbation directly relevant to the minimax value.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditioning on the isolated set reduces RDIM to a complete-randomization contrast for a random subpopulation, but unconditioning restores random support, reciprocal treatment/control denominators, and representativeness bias for the population total effect. Existing dependency-graph CLTs and network-HAC results begin with fixed exposure indicators or Horvitz-Thompson/Hajek weights, not a random greedy maximal independent set. The missing first step is uniform stabilization of the random denominator and conditional variance over the rule library before passing from a conditional CLT to an unconditional, studentized result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform finite-population theorem giving a studentized RDIM limit law under explicit graph and weight conditions, a computable asymptotically conservative variance estimator, and confidence-interval coverage valid for any graph-only selected or randomized WRI mixture.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A surveyed friendship network need not equal the true directed interference graph. Existing misspecification work establishes bias and the exponential cost of naive edge-set enumeration, while partial-network work averages exposures over a model but does not provide exact finite-population WRI design risk. The first WRI proof step that changes is graph-specific isolation: changing one candidate edge changes the conflict graph, the isolated-set distribution, and every dense risk matrix. Maximizing already-computed fixed-graph matrices is therefore invalid; a robust result requires a separation oracle, a compact uncertainty representation, or a joint decomposition state that tracks unresolved edges.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A robust-design theorem and algorithm returning a WRI-rule mixture that minimizes certified RDIM bias-plus-variance over a specified graph-uncertainty class, with either polynomial or FPT complexity under explicit structure or a matching hardness frontier.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proposal characterizes equality between a restricted independent-design class and its unrestricted benchmark through finite feasibility over assignment and response orbits. For WRI, the first proof step changes because the restricted object is the convex hull of finitely many dense risk matrices, whereas the unrestricted benchmark ranges over priority-weight rules or isolation distributions not represented by that hull. Equality needs a graph-specific separation or orbit-compression theorem; failure needs an explicit bounded-treewidth graph with a certified strict gap. Track A contained no paper metadata close enough to support reliable exemplar designation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient convex-hull or dual-separation characterization of equality between finite-library and unrestricted WRI minimax risks, or a smallest graph family with a quantitatively certified strict risk gap.

literature_map:
Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet (2015, AEJ: Applied, doi:10.1257/app.20130442) establish knowledge-diffusion spillovers in the rural-China insurance experiment and motivate a universal-versus-none total-effect target.
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA) and Aronow and Samii (2017, AOAS) anchor finite-population spillover estimands, exposure mappings, and design-based inverse-probability inference.
Ugander et al. (2013, KDD, arXiv:1305.6979) introduce graph-cluster randomization and show how graph structure controls exposure probabilities and variance.
Ugander and Yin (2023, JCI, arXiv:2009.02297) randomize clustering, estimate probabilities by offline resampling, and establish NP-hardness for exact 3-net exposure probabilities on general graphs.
Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi (2024, ICLR, arXiv:2312.04026) use greedy independent sets to disentangle treatment and spillover exposure but target different contrasts and not exact random-greedy risk matrices.
Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li (2024, arXiv:2408.15670) are the direct WRI/RDIM anchor: directed full-neighborhood interference and total effects, with weight choice based on a surrogate rather than exact dense risk.
Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) use an estimand-specific conflict graph for spectral risk rates and conservative inference but do not analyze weighted random isolation.
Li et al. (2023, arXiv:2309.00141) mix Bernoulli and cluster randomization for total effects, showing the value of mixtures without solving a finite WRI-library minimax game.
Viviano et al. (2026, ICLR, arXiv:2310.14983) optimize worst-case cluster-design MSE through min-cut and SDP methods and illustrate the problem on Cai et al.'s China network; their criterion differs from exact WRI/RDIM risk.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) develop conflict-graph minimax theory over designs and estimators but do not provide the proposed finite-library exact-risk certificate.
Gao and Ding (2025, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106119) and Chin (2018, arXiv:1804.03105) provide nearby design-based covariance and CLT machinery; random WRI support and reciprocal denominators remain outside their arguments.
Eiben et al. (2019, Algorithmica, doi:10.1007/s00453-018-0496-4) show that exact relative-order counting has a representation-sensitive FPT versus hardness boundary, making the separator-compression claim nonroutine.
Tropp (2012, FoCM, arXiv:1004.4389) supplies operator-norm matrix concentration, but no located work propagates simultaneous WRI risk-matrix regions into a causal-design optimality gap.
Weinstein and Nevo (2026, Biometrics, doi:10.1093/biomtc/ujag023) and Wilkins-Reeves et al. (2026, UAI, arXiv:2406.11940) show that friendship-network uncertainty is statistically consequential and computationally nontrivial, motivating robust WRI beyond a fixed graph.
